transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm Tom. I... I guess I'm here because of my eating. It's... well, once I start eating, I just can't seem to stop. It's like my hands just keep reaching for more, even when I'm telling myself to stop. It's... it's a bit scary, honestly.
After you eat a lot, do you ever make yourself sick, exercise excessively, or go without food to try to control your weight or the effects of eating?
...Yes. Sometimes. I just... I'll go to the bathroom after and... make myself bring it back up. And, well, I've taken laxatives, too. I just... I get scared of all that food just staying inside me.
How often do you find yourself eating a large amount of food in a short period, and do you feel like you can't stop once you start?

I don't keep an exact count. Just... mostly on those afternoons when I'm alone at the house. It's... well, I can go through a whole loaf of bread. Peanut butter... cookies, whatever leftovers are around, ice cream. Just all in one sitting. I don't even really look up until it's done. I just can't stop it.

Can you tell me how you feel during these episodes? Specifically, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or stop yourself once you start? And do you do anything else after these episodes besides making yourself sick or using laxatives?

...Yeah. Like I said, I just can't stop it. It's out of my hands. 

And after... well. I guess sometimes I just won't eat the next day. I'll make myself skip breakfast, and lunch. And... I try to work it off, I suppose. I'll go outside and do yard chores, or just walk laps. I just keep doing it, way past when my knees and my back are telling me to quit. I just... I keep going.
How often do these episodes happen—like the times when you eat a lot and then make yourself sick or use laxatives after?

...Well, I keep a food log. And... if you look at it, for many months now, it's... it's nearly every week. 

There's usually at least one afternoon where I just... eat out of control. And then I try to make up for it after. By making myself sick, or taking the laxatives... or, like I said, the fasting and pushing myself with the walking and the chores. So... at least once a week, I suppose.
When you make yourself sick or use laxatives, is it usually because you feel uncomfortably full after eating?

Well... yes, partly because I'm too full. But... mostly it's just... I get scared. Scared that all that food is just going to stay inside me. So I go to the bathroom and... make myself bring it back up. Or I take the pills. I just... I have to get it out.
When you make yourself sick or use laxatives, is it mainly because you're worried about gaining weight or how your body looks?
...I suppose so. I just... I don't want to get heavy. I don't like thinking about it.
Do you usually make yourself sick or use laxatives specifically to prevent gaining weight after eating a lot?

...Yes. Like I said before, I... I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it up. Or I take the laxatives. I just... I get scared it's all going to stay in me and turn into weight. So I have to get it out.
Do you usually make yourself sick or use laxatives only after eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period of time?

Yes... I suppose so. When I'm alone at the house on those afternoons... I can get through quite a bit. A whole loaf of bread... peanut butter, cookies. Whatever leftovers are around... ice cream. I just... I eat it all in one sitting before I even really look up. And then... well, yes.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives right after those afternoons when you eat a lot, or does it sometimes happen at other times too?
...Just after. I don't... I don't do it otherwise. Just when I've eaten all that.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives within a couple of hours after those afternoons when you eat a lot, or does it sometimes happen much later?
...It's usually right after. I don't wait around. Just... within an hour or so, I suppose.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives even when you don't feel uncomfortably full, or do you usually do it because you feel too full?
...I couldn't really tell you. I don't... I don't pay much mind to how my stomach feels, exactly. I just... do it.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives even when you don’t feel physically full, just because you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating?
...I don't know. I suppose... I just do it because I ate all that. I don't really think about the control part. It's just what happens next.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives even when you don't feel physically full, just because you feel like you've eaten too much or lost control over your eating?

...I suppose so. I just... if I eat too much, I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. Or I take the laxatives. I just... I get scared the food is going to stay in me, so I have to get rid of it. That's all.
When you make yourself sick or take laxatives, is it mainly because you’re afraid of gaining weight, or because you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating?
...I don't really know. I don't sit and think about the reasons why. I just... I just know I can't keep it down. That's all.
Do you usually make yourself sick or take laxatives only after you've had one of those out-of-control eating episodes, or do you sometimes do it even when you haven't eaten a lot?

...I thought we just went over this. It's... mostly just after I eat too much. That's when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. Or take the laxatives. Like I said, I just get scared the food is going to stay in me. I don't really keep track of exactly how much I ate beforehand... just if it feels like too much.
Is the main reason you make yourself sick or take laxatives because you’re afraid of gaining weight, or is it more because you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating?
...You just asked me that. I told you, I don't really know. I just... I don't want it inside me. That's it.
